newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil seen issuing more bonds in 1997 - Cenbank.
newsitem.headline: Brazil seen issuing more bonds in 1997 - Cenbank.

text.p: Brazil is likely to issue more bonds this year as international markets continue to show an appetite for new issues, a Brazilian central bank official said on Monday.

"We are likely to issue more bonds this year. There is no reason for not taking advantage of the markets' favorable conditions," Central Bank International Affairs Director Gustavo Franco told reporters.
Earlier this year Brazil launched a 1.0 billion 10-year Deutsche mark bond.
Brazil is in a comfortable situation because financing is not the country's main reason for tapping foreign markets, Franco said after addressing a conference on Latin American utilities.
"The best issuer is one which does not need (the funds raised with the issue)," he said. He added that Brazil was issuing new debt to increase its exposure to foreign markets.
